title: Bilateral exchange in synthetic biology: experiences, challenges, and opportunities for training and research
content:
Abstract
Synthetic biology and the emerging field of biomanufacturing provide new research concepts that should be incorporated into the training of the next generation of scientists. Key elements of synthetic biology are the standardization, modularization, and characterization of biological parts. Defined parts can be assembled into functional transcription units to pathways of multiple units, chromosomes, and/or whole genomes. Here, we highlight the importance of global exchange and state-of-the-art training in the Global South to empower research and reduce the gap between countries. Based on initial seed funding, we established a multidisciplinary bilateral exchange program between Germany and Colombia, including lecture series, experimental workshops, and bilateral exchanges in training and research. The elements are adaptable and our hands-on courses can be carried out with limited resources while covering aspects of synthetic biology. Importantly, this initiative will allow early-career researchers to build an international network, opening up opportunities in research collaboration and paving the way for greater equity.
